offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: Since the v2 deploy, every webhook the receiver gets is rejected as bad_signature and none are queued. That matches the alert's growing count of unacknowledged webhooks.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 19:11:49 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs its webhooks with the secret the receiver used before, so every incoming webhook now fails signature verification. The receiver rejects each one as bad_signature and does not acknowledge it, and nothing new reaches provider-events. The provider keeps resending unacknowledged webhooks, so incoming traffic climbs steeply: about 26/s by 19:13, all of it bad_signature. Because the backlog of unacknowledged webhooks only grows (186 at the alert), the money check cannot settle up to its cutoff, and BooksBehindProvider fires. The consumers, Kafka and the database look healthy; the break is at the receiver's signature check.

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy. webhook-receiver alone was restarted later, at 19:11:50, after the rest of the stack started around 19:10:22-30.
The newest deploy is webhook-receiver at 19:11:49 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. No other service changed after startup.
The total webhook receive rate rises sharply after 19:11:49, from about 3.7/s to about 25/s. This fits the provider resending webhooks that were not acknowledged.

Before 19:11:53 every webhook was queued. After the deploy, the bad_signature series appears and grows to about 26/s, while queued falls toward zero (1.46/s at 19:12:23, then no further points). Every webhook is now rejected at the signature check.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines, so the signature rejections are not logged at warning level. The metrics are the only place they show.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to the settings it had before the 19:11:49 deploy, i.e. the previous WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION, so it again verifies with the secret the provider actually signs with. The provider will then redeliver the backlog of unacknowledged webhooks, the receiver will queue them, and the consumers will catch up. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm the books settle. Re-attempt the v2 rotation only in step with the provider, for example by accepting both secrets during the rotation.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver is recreated, so it pauses briefly during the restart. The provider keeps resending during that pause, so no webhooks are lost. When the receiver comes back, the redelivered backlog causes a burst of events on provider-events. The ledger-consumer runs in idempotent mode, and the confirmer matches events by our id, so redeliveries should not double-book. Not yet verified: whether some events were queued under v2 but still fail later. If v2 was meant to be the provider's new secret, the rollback could break verification again.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes signature failures worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, then coordinate the correct secret with the provider side. Watch klaxon_webhooks_received_total by result: after the rollback, queued should rise and bad_signature should drop to zero.
